speaker: Patient
text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). The rapid onset of focal neurological deficits (right leg weakness, gait instability) combined with progressive cognitive decline (forgetfulness, getting lost) and behavioral changes (paranoia, agitation) in a 44-year-old male suggests a demyelinating process affecting the white matter, possibly due to an underlying immunocompromised state. I will proceed to order MRI of the brain to confirm the presence of non-enhancing, multifocal white matter lesions.
